column1: # The same questions, phrased the way a person types them.
# DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER. Every row rewrites a row of
# queries.tsv and keeps its expected answer exactly; only the wording moves,
# toward how somebody actually asks. A query must still never contain its own
# answer's name — the rule matters more here, not less, because filler makes it
# easy to smuggle one in.
# See `tests/eval/fixture/queries_natural.tsv` for why the band exists. This is
# the app-shaped half of it: the fixture corpus is 22 dense units, and whether
# phrasing costs anything on a real Rails app is a different question.
how do I suspend an account that has been misbehaving
is there something that blocks federation with a whole domain
what do I call to approve a follow request that is pending
how do I generate a backup archive of all of an account's data
where is the code that recalculates which hashtags are trending
is there anything that redirects an old permalink to where it now lives
how does a new toot get pushed into the home feeds of followers
# --- no token shared with the answer's identifier ----------------------------
how do I look up who an @user@server address actually belongs to
what builds the timeline you see when you first open the app
is there something that decides whether this visitor may read this post
how do I keep a toot out of a follower's stream when it fails the rules
what caps how often one user is allowed to repeat an action
how do we notice an instance has been unreachable for days and give up
is there anything that strips the markup out of a status for a preview
where do I get the canonical web address of a remote user's profile
what tells me whether this login looks risky
how do we prove an incoming federation message came from its author
# --- behaviour that appears in NO identifier ---------------------------------
is there something that reopens a dropped connection and tries once more
how do I make sure two workers never run the same critical section at once
what treats a login from the same subnet as one we have already seen
how do the viewer-specific fields get filled into a cached toot payload
